title: Deep Mesoscopic Dynamics
authors: Yue Zhao, Shiqi Wu, Yihang Ouyang, Sergey Grebenchuk, Magdalena Grzeszczyk, Xiaoxu Zhao, Kostya S. Novoselov, Maciej Koperski, Qianxiao Li
abstract: Microscopic simulations resolve spatial patterns but are feasible only over small domains and short timescales, whereas bulk descriptions erase those patterns through spatial averaging. Mesoscopic fields preserve this spatial organisation, but their effective equations are known only for selected microscopic systems and scaling limits. We introduce Deep Mesoscopic Dynamics (DeepMesoD), which uses neural networks to learn an effective mesoscopic field equation from microscopic trajectories at a prescribed coarse-graining scale. For the nonconserved dissipative dynamics studied here, DeepMesoD learns the free-energy functional with a spatial interaction kernel and a state-dependent dissipation operator constrained by the fluctuation-dissipation relation. We first validate the construction in the Ising-Kac model, where the learned mesoscopic equation recovers the known hydrodynamic limit and rollouts remain stable far beyond the training horizon. We then treat two systems without closed-form mesoscopic descriptions. For a two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet governed by atomistic spin dynamics, DeepMesoD learns a mesoscopic model whose predictions match atomistic references up to 1 ns, and a rollout with an unseen initial condition remains bounded up to 25 ns. For layered CrBr$_3$, the learned kernel captures the suppression and sign reversal of interlayer coupling at a stacking fault whose location and strength are not supplied as inputs. Controlled changes to the learned interaction show how fault number and placement shape multistep magnetic responses, complementing our magneto-photoluminescence measurements. Across the two atomistic systems, DeepMesoD achieves a three-to-four-order-of-magnitude reduction in wall-clock time compared with atomistic spin dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces DeepMesoD, a neural network method that learns effective mesoscopic field equations directly from microscopic simulations. It bridges the gap between detailed, slow microscopic models and overly simplified bulk descriptions by preserving crucial spatial patterns. The method is shown to accurately model diverse magnetic systems, offering dramatic speedups while capturing complex physics like domain wall interactions.
main_problem: To develop efficient methods to simulate mesoscopic dynamics that accurately resolve spatial patterns, bridging the gap between computationally limited microscopic simulations and pattern-erasing bulk descriptions.
main_result: The DeepMesoD framework successfully learns effective mesoscopic field equations for complex magnetic systems, achieving massive computational speedups while accurately reproducing known physical limits and capturing subtle material effects like interlayer coupling changes.
method: A novel neural network approach (DeepMesoD) is used to learn the effective mesoscopic field equation directly from microscopic trajectories, constrained by fundamental physical principles like the fluctuation-dissipation relation.
model_or_system: The study applies to general dissipative dynamics, focusing on magnetic systems like the Ising-Kac model, 2D Heisenberg ferromagnets, and layered CrBr3 films. The dynamics are modeled via stochastic field equations incorporating learned free-energy functionals and dissipation operators.
key_observables: Mesoscopic field evolution, free-energy functional, dissipation operator, spectral power, and correlation rates.
important_parameters: Coarse-graining scale, temperature (T=0.75, T=1.5), and fault geometry/placement in layered materials.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are assumed to belong to a general class of dissipative dynamics satisfying the fluctuation-dissipation relation; the learned model assumes locality for certain interaction factors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow from microscopic to mesoscopic learning, show the recovery of known hydrodynamic limits, and demonstrate the ability to model complex fault structures in layered magnets.
paper_structure: The paper introduces DeepMesoD, validates it on the Ising-Kac model, extends it to the Heisenberg ferromagnet, and applies it to layered CrBr3, detailing the mathematical constraints and the computational efficiency gains.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, data-driven tool for simulating complex, non-equilibrium dynamics in condensed matter systems where traditional analytical or purely microscopic methods fail due to computational cost or complexity.
